notes:
**Collaboration grows up.** Shared projects stop being read-only windows into someone else's work — you can contribute to them, see who did what, and keep your own things when a share ends.

## Roles you can actually read

- **Viewer, Contributor, Planner** — permissions have names now, and they say what someone can do in plain words instead of describing a tier.
- **The invite says what you'll get** — the role named in the invitation is the role you see once you accept, worded the same way in both places.

## Contribute, don't just watch

- **Add tasks to a shared project** — a Contributor can create work in a project someone shared with them, and it lands in the owner's Keen the same as anything else.
- **Edit shared projects and milestones** — names, descriptions, dates and status are editable to the extent your role allows, not just tasks.
- **See who changed what** — shared rows carry edit attribution, and you can see who's working alongside you right now.

## Your work outlives the share

- **Losing access no longer loses your work.** When a shared item goes out of reach — the owner removes it, or simply stops sharing it — the item stays in your Keen with everything you hung on it: your tags, notes, reminders, favorites and knowledge links.
- **It says what it knows, and no more.** A shared item that goes quiet tells you it's no longer available to you. It doesn't claim the other person deleted anything, because from here that genuinely can't be told apart from them un-sharing it.

## Invites that look like Keen

- **Branded invitation emails** and a landing page that matches the app, end to end.
- **Sign-in errors say what went wrong** instead of showing "Unknown error".

---

**Updating:** Keen updates itself — you'll be prompted on next launch, or check Settings → Updates.

**Managed servers:** this release updates the backend too. If you're on a managed server, Keen will ask you to update it after the app restarts; that takes about a minute.
